title: Tightness of a Sequence of Measures

content:
\begin{defbox}{14.3}
\end{defbox}

A sequence of probability measures .(Pn)\infty

n=1 on R is said to be tight if for all

\epsilon> 0, there exists a sufficiently large M\epsilon such that

Pn([-M\epsilon,M\epsilon])> 1 - \epsilon for all n.

Similarly, a sequence of cdf .(Fn)\infty

n=1 is said to be tight if for any \epsilon> 0 there

exists M\epsilon such that Fn(M\epsilon)- F n(-M\epsilon)> 1- \epsilon for all n.
